claim: HPQ sand is made into fused-quartz crucibles used in the Czochralski (CZ) process to grow silicon ingots; the quartz is not the chip.

evidence.quote: for the manufacture of fused quartz crucibles used in the Czochralski (CZ) process

evidence.locator: USGS MCS 2026 Quartz, Domestic Production and Use
evidence.quote: fused quartz crucibles (for manufacturing silicon metal ingots that are later processed into silicon wafers for the photovoltaic cell and semiconductor markets)
Quartz crucibles are a critical component in the manufacture of photovoltaic cells and semiconductor chips.

method: Read three independent publishers (two companies, USGS).
notes: Same quartz also goes to fibre optics, lamp tubing, specialty glass (USGS).

claim: USGS definition of HPQ: under 100 ppm total impurities (99.99%); ultra-high-purity under 10 ppm (99.999%); Spruce Pine HPQ is >99.999% pure.

evidence.quote: Ground high-purity quartz (HPQ) is generally defined as natural quartz containing less than 100 parts per million (ppm) of total impurities, equivalent to a purity level of 99.99%.
compared with the greater than 99.999% pure HPQ that is sourced from Spruce Pine, NC
99.999% pure silica

notes: The 'greater than 99.999%' for Spruce Pine is USGS reporting a figure from Chinese-announcement coverage ('It was reported that...'), not a USGS measurement. Company grade sheets (IOTA ppm per element) are not public in what I could open: UNVERIFIED.

claim: Sibelco and TQC publish no silicon process temperature; TQC states quartz melting point 1,723 C; silicon melts at 1414 C (US DOE labs).

evidence.quote: 1,723° C melting point of quartz
This process occurs at extremely high temperatures under tightly controlled conditions

notes: Company pages give no number for the silicon melt. Silicon 1414 C is from Jefferson Lab / LANL via PubChem; not the CZ pulling temperature as such.

claim: TQC: a full ingot can weigh over 500 kg and measure 4.3 m long with a 25 cm diameter; one quartz crucible can pull approximately 8 ingots over a 400 hour period.

evidence.quote: A full ingot can weigh over 500 kg and measure 4.3 m long with a 25 cm diameter. One quartz crucible can pull approximately 8 ingots over a 400 hour period.

The page does not say semiconductor vs solar for these figures (it speaks of ingots as base for wafers 'in photovoltaic cells and semiconductors'). What happens to the crucible after use: NOT STATED on the page (UNVERIFIED).

claim: TQC: one 300 mm silicon ingot can be used to manufacture approximately 2 million semiconductor chips.

evidence.quote: One 300 mm silicon ingot can be used to manufacture approximately 2 million semiconductor chips

notes: COMPANY SAYS; no method given, no chip size/type. Different ingot from the 25 cm one in C04. Do not narrate as measured fact.

claim: Spruce Pine HPQ district geology: USGS 1962 puts the alaskite and associated pegmatite at 'early Paleozoic' age.

evidence.quote: large bodies of alaskite and associated pegmatite of early Paleozoic age

notes: Dated 1962; PP577 (1968) calls the related Whiteside granite 'Paleozoic(?)' with lead-alpha ages 358-708 Ma 'not definitive'. Quartz is 'an extremely small part' of 1962 district output.

claim: Intrusions of the Spruce Pine district range 377-404 Ma; the most reliable U-Pb zircon ID-TIMS ages are ~377 Ma (Devonian).

evidence.locator: K. G. Stewart, UNC Chapel Hill, GSA Southeastern Section abstract 2012
evidence.quote: Ages for the intrusions range from 377 Ma to 404 Ma but the most reliable ages (U-Pb zircon ID-TIMS) are ~377 Ma.
The Devonian ages match the timing of the Acadian orogeny

method: Conference abstract by a geologist at UNC; peer-reviewed journal paper (e.g. Swanson & Veal 2010) not reached.
notes: So '~380 million years / Devonian' is supportable as 'about 377 million years' for the granodioritic intrusions that host the pegmatites. Brief cited 'Swanson 2012 Canadian Mineralogist, Mineralogy of Spruce Pine pegmatites': I could not find that title; the 2012 Can. Mineral. paper by Swanson is on the Tin-Spodumene Belt (different place).

claim: Company geology versions differ: Sibelco says district created about 380 million years ago when Africa collided with North America, pure thanks to a lack of water; TQC says the Appalachians formed 350 million years ago and the magma came from melted ocean sediments that cooled slowly.

evidence.quote: Geologists calculate that the Spruce Pine mining district was created about 380 million years ago when Africa collided with North America.
The purity of Spruce Pine’s quartz is thanks to a lack of water where all the friction occurred, preventing the introduction of multiple impurities.
350 million years ago the Appalachians were formed
Ocean sediments melted as a result and created the magma that would slowly cool to form the Spruce Pine pegmatites almost free from inclusions.

notes: Two companies, two explanations (dry vs slow-cooled subduction melt). 'Waterless magma cooled slowly' is a blend; neither company and no source I opened uses that wording. Use: 'Sibelco says...'. No peer-reviewed purity-mechanism paper opened: UNVERIFIED as science.

claim: No primary source states a percentage share of world HPQ for Spruce Pine. USGS says world production data 'was not available' and names the US as leader.

evidence.quote: World Mine Production and Reserves:10 This information was not available.
The United States was estimated to be the leader in production of HPQ with other sources being Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, India, and Russia.
Our investment will ensure that Spruce Pine remains the world’s leading source of HPQ.

method: Read USGS MCS 2025 and 2026 quartz chapters, Sibelco and TQC pages and news; searched EU CRM 2023 (HPQ not a listed item in what I reached), no share found.
notes: The '70-90%, up to 95%' figure: only seen in secondary pieces (search summaries of Wikipedia mirror, SCMP 'experts say 80 to 90 per cent', BloombergNEF 80% via press). CRU (a vendor, banned) says Sibelco+TQC+Pacific Quartz together had 'around 85% market share in 2023' (A42) - that includes a CHINESE producer, so it is not a Spruce Pine share. USGS 2026 also notes China announced 35 Mt HPQ reserves (tests 99.995-99.998%). Recommend: narrate 'the world's leading source, by the companies' own account; nobody publishes the exact share'.

issued : {'date-parts': [[1918, 11, 1]]}

claim: The pen-in-molten-tin story: TQC tells it as fact. The earliest telling I found is a web article by P. Tomaszewski (quoted by a Kiel University course page); no document by Czochralski himself was found.

evidence.quote: When he dipped his pen in molten tin instead of an inkwell he discovered that the strand of tin he drew out was a single crystal.
instead of dipping his pen in the inkpot, he dipped it in the crucible and withdrew it quickly

method: Chain: TQC page (company) -> (no cite). Kiel page -> Tomaszewski web article (rekt.pol.lublin.pl/~ptwk/art2.htm) -> his sources unknown. IUCr newsletter vol 28 no 3 and Springer MRS 2004 article blocked (403/challenge).
notes: Details differ between tellings: TQC 'pen in molten tin instead of an inkwell'; Tomaszewski 'one evening ... left aside a crucible with molten tin'. Narrate as 'the story goes', never as documented. 1916 date = manuscript date per Tomaszewski-derived page A17 (secondary).

claim: First pulled single crystals in electronics: Teal and Little at Bell Labs (germanium, 1950, Phys. Rev. 78, 647); silicon crystals followed at Texas Instruments (Teal, announced 1954 IRE meeting).

evidence.quote: Teal, Gordon K. and Little, John B. "Growth of Germanium Single Crystals,"
Based on techniques developed in 1917 by the Polish chemist Jan Czochralski, he suspended a small "seed" crystal of germanium in a crucible of molten germanium and slowly withdrew it
Gordon announced the breakthrough at the 1954 meeting of the Institute of Radio Engineers in Dayton, Ohio

method: CHM (museum) and NAS Biographical Memoir; Physical Review paper itself not opened.
notes: So 'Teal and Little ~1950' was GERMANIUM; silicon pulling by Teal's group at TI (1952 move, 1954 announcement). CHM says 'techniques developed in 1917' (conflicts with 1918 print date). Teal & Buehler 1952 silicon paper citation unverified.
